objectives: Describe what IGCSE ICT 0417 involves.
Complete a diagnostic document task.
Set improvement targets for the term.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Baseline WPM and accuracy run.

plan.title: The IGCSE pathway
plan.detail: Walk through the 0417 specification overview: practical papers, the kinds of task, why following a brief exactly matters more than creativity here.

plan.title: Diagnostic task
plan.detail: A Year 8 level document task under timed conditions: headings, a table, an image, saved to a named file. Mark against a simplified rubric.

plan.title: Gap analysis
plan.detail: Return the marks with the rubric. Each pupil identifies two specific gaps - not 'be better' but 'I lost marks for file naming'.

plan.title: Targets
plan.detail: Write two targets in the front of the exercise book, to be reviewed in Week 10. Log out.

successCriteria: I completed the diagnostic in the time.
I identified two specific gaps from the rubric.
My targets are written and measurable.

objectives: Format a document to a precise written brief.
Use columns, a drop cap and a pull quote.
Control margins and page breaks.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Read the brief twice
plan.detail: Model the IGCSE habit: read, highlight every instruction, tick each as you complete it. Marks come from compliance, not flair.

plan.title: Columns and features
plan.detail: Two columns with a specified gutter, a drop cap on the opening paragraph, a pull quote in a text box.

plan.title: Page control
plan.detail: Set exact margins, insert page breaks before each heading, and use 'keep with next' so headings never sit alone at the bottom of a page.

plan.title: Brief audit
plan.detail: Swap and tick off every instruction on a partner's work. Any untick loses a mark. Log out.

activities: Columns, drop cap and pull quote
successCriteria: My document meets every instruction in the brief.
My columns, drop cap and pull quote are correctly formatted.
No heading is stranded at the bottom of a page.

objectives: Set up a mail merge from a spreadsheet data source.
Insert merge fields into a document.
Produce personalised certificates for a whole class.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why mail merge
plan.detail: One template plus one data file equals 30 personalised documents. Ask how long 30 by hand would take - that is the point.

plan.title: Prepare the data
plan.detail: Build the source spreadsheet: FirstName, LastName, Class, Award. Clean headers, no blank rows - a messy source breaks the merge.

plan.title: Run the merge
plan.detail: Start Mail Merge, select recipients, insert merge fields into the certificate template, preview results, finish and merge.

plan.title: Troubleshoot
plan.detail: Common faults: extra spaces around fields, wrong data file selected, fields showing as codes. Log out.

successCriteria: My data source has clean headers and no blank rows.
My template uses merge fields, not typed names.
I produced personalised certificates for the whole list.

resources.label: Kevin Stratvert - Mail Merge in Word

objectives: Explain the terms table, field and record.
Choose appropriate data types for fields.
Design a database for a real scenario.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Tables, fields, records
plan.detail: Use a printed class register: the whole sheet is the table, a column is a field, a row is a record. Then map it onto the database software.

plan.title: Data types
plan.detail: Text, number, date, currency, boolean. Why store a phone number as text? Because you never do arithmetic with it and leading zeros matter.

plan.title: Design on paper
plan.detail: Choose a scenario - class library, sports fixtures, cafe menu. Design the table: field names, data types, which field is the primary key.

plan.title: Build the structure
plan.detail: Create the table in Access or Base and enter three test records. Log out.

activities: Paper design then build the table
successCriteria: I can define table, field and record.
Every field in my design has an appropriate data type.
I built the table and entered test records.

objectives: Write a query with criteria.
Combine criteria with AND and OR.
Add a validation rule to a field.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Asking questions of data
plan.detail: A query is a question. 'Show all fiction books' becomes criteria on the Genre field. Demo the query grid: field, show, criteria.

plan.title: Three queries
plan.detail: Build: one single-criterion query, one using AND (fiction AND after 2010), one using OR. Run each and check the results make sense.

plan.title: Validation rules
plan.detail: Add a rule such as Year between 1900 and 2026, with a helpful validation message. Test it by entering 1850 - the rejection is the proof.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Why is validation better than trusting the typist? Log out.

activities: Add and test a validation rule
successCriteria: My queries return the right records.
I used AND and OR criteria correctly.
My validation rule blocks invalid data and explains why.

objectives: Generate a formatted report from a database.
Group records under headings.
Add running totals and a cover page.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: From raw data to a report
plan.detail: Show a raw table dump versus a grouped, formatted report. The data is the same - presentation is what makes it usable.

plan.title: Build the report
plan.detail: Report wizard: choose fields, group by a sensible field, sort within groups. Then edit the layout in design view.

plan.title: Totals and cover
plan.detail: Add a count or sum in the group footer. Add a cover page with title, your name and the date.

plan.title: Export and check
plan.detail: Export to PDF and check the layout survived. Log out.

activities: Add totals and export to PDF
successCriteria: My report groups records under clear headings.
It shows a total or count per group.
The PDF export keeps the layout intact.

objectives: Complete an IGCSE-style task in 30 minutes.
Follow a written brief exactly.
Save with the exact file name required.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: How examiners mark
plan.detail: Walk through a mark scheme: marks for each specified feature, nothing for extras. Creativity that ignores the brief scores zero.

plan.title: Timed task
plan.detail: 30-minute specimen-style practical. Strict timing, brief on paper, no discussion.

plan.title: Mark it yourself
plan.detail: Swap and mark against the actual mark scheme. Award marks strictly - being generous helps nobody.

plan.title: Where marks went
plan.detail: Class tally of the most commonly missed marks. Usually file naming and one small formatting instruction. Log out.

successCriteria: I finished the task within 30 minutes.
My file name matches the brief exactly.
I marked a peer's work strictly against the scheme.

objectives: Improve my timed task against the mark scheme.
Apply the habit: read the brief twice before starting.
Save in the required format and name.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Read twice, then start
plan.detail: Practise the routine: read, highlight instructions, plan the order of work, then open the software. Two minutes of planning saves ten of rework.

plan.title: Refine the Week 7 task
plan.detail: Return to the task and recover every lost mark: layout, spelling, file name, save format.

plan.title: Format matters
plan.detail: Save as .docx, then as PDF, then as .rtf. Discuss when a brief specifies a format and why it matters to the client.

plan.title: Re-mark
plan.detail: Re-mark the improved version. Record both scores to see the gain. Log out.

successCriteria: My improved version scores higher than the first attempt.
I saved in the exact format the brief required.
I can describe my read-the-brief routine.

objectives: Choose a scenario for the combined document and database piece.
Draft the document to a brief I write myself.
Identify what the database must store.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Pick a real client
plan.detail: Scenarios with a real audience: the school library, a sports day, the canteen. Better work comes from a real user.

plan.title: Write your own brief
plan.detail: Write the brief the way an examiner would: specific, measurable instructions. You will be marked against your own brief.

plan.title: Draft the document
plan.detail: Apply advanced layout from Week 2: columns, styles, captioned images.

plan.title: Database fields
plan.detail: List the fields the database will need and their data types. Log out.

successCriteria: My scenario has a real audience.
My brief lists specific, checkable instructions.
My document draft uses advanced layout features.

objectives: Practise all four assessed skills under time pressure.
Peer-check against an IGCSE-style rubric.
Review my Week 1 targets.

plan.title: Station briefing
plan.detail: Four stations, 15 minutes each, rubric at every station.

plan.title: Station 1 - Advanced layout
plan.detail: Columns, drop cap, pull quote, exact margins, to a written brief.

plan.title: Station 2 - Database query
plan.detail: Two queries with AND/OR criteria on a supplied database.

plan.title: Station 3 - Mail merge
plan.detail: Merge a supplied data file into a template and produce the output.

plan.title: Station 4 - Timed brief
plan.detail: A short brief with an exact file name and save format.

plan.title: Target review
plan.detail: Return to the Week 1 targets. Met, partly met or not yet? Set one target for the exam. Log out.

activities: Peer marking against the IGCSE rubric
successCriteria: I completed all four stations in the time.
My peer marking matched the rubric.
I reviewed my Week 1 targets honestly.

objectives: Follow an IGCSE-style brief for 90 minutes.
Produce an advanced document plus a database query and report.
Save every file exactly as specified.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Read twice, highlight every instruction. Exact file names on the board. Silent conditions.

plan.title: Document section
plan.detail: Advanced layout to the brief: columns, styles, captioned image, header and footer.

plan.title: Database section
plan.detail: Build or use the supplied table, run the specified queries, generate the report.

plan.title: Combine and export
plan.detail: Bring the database output into the document as required, then export to the specified format.

plan.title: Submit
plan.detail: Every file named exactly as the brief states, in the assessment folder. Check before logging out.

successCriteria: My document meets every layout instruction.
My queries return the records the brief asked for.
My report is formatted and included.
Every file name matches the brief exactly.

objectives: Build the portfolio document to my own brief.
Include columns, a contents list and captioned images.
Add mail-merge fields for personalisation.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Brief check
plan.detail: Re-read your Week 9 brief and list what is still missing from the draft.

plan.title: Build
plan.detail: Two columns where appropriate, automatic contents list, captioned images, header and footer, merge fields where the document is personalised.

plan.title: Self-audit
plan.detail: Tick every instruction in your own brief. Anything unticked is next lesson's job. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My document meets every instruction in my own brief.
It has a contents list and captioned images.
Merge fields are in place where personalisation is needed.

objectives: Build a database with at least 15 records.
Apply validation to at least one field.
Write three queries that answer questions from the brief.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Structure before data
plan.detail: Fix field names, data types and the primary key before typing 15 records - changing them later means retyping.

plan.title: Build and populate
plan.detail: Create the table(s), add validation, and enter at least 15 realistic records. Realistic data makes the queries meaningful.

plan.title: Three queries
plan.detail: Each query must answer a real question from the brief. Write the question above each query.

plan.title: Test the validation
plan.detail: Deliberately enter bad data and confirm it is rejected. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My database has 15 or more records.
At least one field has a working validation rule.
My three queries answer real questions from the brief.

objectives: Combine document and database output into one deliverable.
Produce a client-ready PDF report.
Check the whole package against the brief.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What client-ready means
plan.detail: No placeholder text, consistent fonts, correct dates, a cover page, and nothing that needs explaining. Show a nearly-good example and find its flaws.

plan.title: Combine
plan.detail: Bring the database report into the document (or supply it as a linked appendix). Ensure numbering, headings and captions are consistent throughout.

plan.title: Export and inspect
plan.detail: Export the whole package as PDF and inspect every page as a client would.

plan.title: Brief audit
plan.detail: Final tick-through of the brief. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My package contains no placeholder or leftover text.
Formatting is consistent from cover to last page.
The PDF is ready to hand to a real client.

objectives: Present my work as if to a real client in five minutes.
Demonstrate the database queries live.
Save the complete package to the portfolio.

plan.title: Rehearse the pitch
plan.detail: Structure: here is what you asked for, here is how it works, here are the queries you can run yourself.

plan.title: Client demo day
plan.detail: Five minutes each. Run at least one query live - it is the part that proves the database actually works.

plan.title: Client questions
plan.detail: Audience acts as the client: 'Can it show me only this year's records?' Presenters answer or note it as a future feature.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Document, database file, PDF and brief into the portfolio folder, correctly named.

plan.title: Looking ahead
plan.detail: Which of these skills appears on IGCSE paper tasks? Set one target for Term 2. Log out.

activities: Portfolio save and IGCSE target setting
successCriteria: I presented within five minutes in a client-facing way.
I ran a query live and explained the result.
My complete package is in the portfolio folder.
